brightport_bryma.m: A visitor, how unusual. I assume you haven't simply stumbled upon my cabin by accident?
r: Are you the person named Bryma?
Yuck, what is that thing inside your kitchen?

brightport_bryma0.m: It's an odd coincidence that the only two visitors I have had in years are asking the same question. You two could almost be twins.
r: So you are Bryma. I'm looking for a document from the Brightport archive that was stolen.
Could that possibly have been my brother, Andor?

brightport_bryma1.m: Andor? Yes, I think that was his name.

brightport_bryma10.m: We sat down and he started asking me all sorts of questions. I was glad to have someone to talk to. But soon, he pulled out a list of ingredients and asked about how to acquire and use them. Most which were highly poisonous.

brightport_bryma11.m: I tried to refuse him, but that's when his tone shifted. The cheerful charisma he'd shown vanished. As he pulled out that scroll, I heard him mumbling, 'last resort...'

brightport_bryma12.m: I had no choice but to accept it. I told him everything he wanted to know, and he left me with the scroll before leaving. It might have been useful to me twenty years ago, but I've already researched and developed my baking methods without the need for it.
r: Can we talk about something else?

brightport_bryma13.m: About half a year ago, I was carefully measuring the ingredients for my baking experiments when I heard the door. I went to look, and a boy who looked a little older than you introduced himself as Andor.

brightport_bryma14.m: Sure, what do you want to know?
r: Can you tell me about Andor again?
Why do you live here in the forest?
I'm curious, how did that scroll reach you?
What's with that statue at the entrance of the forest?
You mentioned your bonemeal research, what can you tell me about the potion?
Can you tell me about your bonemeal theory again?

brightport_bryma15.m: I discovered this place in my youth while researching Brightport's fauna. After Lord Geomyr's coronation, many alchemists like myself were at risk of being arrested under the new laws. So I returned here to continue my research.

brightport_bryma16.m: It started in my second year at the academy, at the beginning of my baking studies. I set out to develop a unique leavening method to stand out from other bakers and make a name for myself.

brightport_bryma17.m: I tried using different yeasts, temperatures, and moisture levels, but none gave me the results I was hoping for. On a whim, I decided to mix a bonemeal potion into the process.

brightport_bryma18.m: The application of potions in baking, but primarily bonemeal potions. Their healing potency and various properties puzzled me for many years. I studied them with the great minds of Feygard and Nor City alike.
r: What do potions have to do with baking?

brightport_bryma19.m: To my amazement, the bread rose to nearly triple its size! That's when I brought it to the Headmaster's attention. It was very well received, and I was rewarded with a specially made bonemeal potion from his collection.

brightport_bryma2.m:
You mean the secret scroll that I have right here? 

[Bryma takes out a rolled, tattered looking parchment]
r: You can give it to me, or I can take it by force.
I need to take it back, could you kindly give it to me?

brightport_bryma20.m: But the bread baked using that potion started mutating, much like what you can see in my kitchen. Soon afterward, my research was banned, and I had no choice but to leave if I wanted to continue my studies.
r: Can I ask you something else?
Thanks for telling me this story. I will be on my way.

brightport_bryma21.m: Don't underestimate baking, child. To master this art takes years of arduous training, including the study of advanced alchemy.

brightport_bryma22.m: It will be a long and difficult subject, so please keep that in mind and don't interrupt me.

brightport_bryma23.m: First, what do you think makes bonemeal so potent that people still seek it out despite it now being illegal?
r: Personally I don't know, that evil concoction hasn't been anywhere near my mouth.
I'm not sure, but the main ingredient is easy to find anywhere.

brightport_bryma24.m: I don't know whether to applaud your commitment or waive it off as a form of childish ignorance, but either way...

brightport_bryma25.m: That is true, any ordinary tomb will do for some bones. And monsters are not an uncommon appearance in our day and age.

brightport_bryma26.m: The answer would be all the correct reasons you could cite. It's cheap, it's effective, and it worked for hundreds of years.

brightport_bryma27.m: That simple answer is the closest to the correct one. And I would have told you the same, had I not dedicated my life to it.

brightport_bryma28.m: But if you think I'm a blind supporter of its use, you're mistaken. In the first place, don't you think there's something off about it? It's easy to make and immensely effective.

brightport_bryma29.m: Not to mention that the origin of those bones could have very well have been human. There have been stories of such things having been done, especially during plagues...
r: I thought we would be talking about your research?

brightport_bryma3.m: He brought me a scroll, and in exchange, he wanted me to mentor him in alchemy.
r: I was looking for that scroll, can I have it?
You can give that scroll to me, or I can take it by force.

brightport_bryma30.m: Oh right, my apologies. I got a bit sidetracked. Yes, where do I begin.

brightport_bryma31.m: In my baking research, I discovered that the potion does not merely heal but it facilitates growth. What we perceive as healing is, in fact, simply the acceleration of the body's natural regeneration condensed into a shorter time by the potion.

brightport_bryma32.m: But my experiments revealed something more. The late Headmaster Dervin rewarded me with an advanced bonemeal potion that contained a mysterious ingredient called kazarite, which doubled the potency of a regular potion.

brightport_bryma33.m: This completely changed my perspective. When I asked for the recipe to identify the ingredient responsible, I was denied. But it was no setback. I soon realized that bones are not unique in their properties. It's common alchemical knowledge that monster parts are prime ingredients for potions, but my discoveries went even further.

brightport_bryma34.m: I call this the Theory of Essence. We all know that when the Rift opened, immense magical energy entered our plane along with the monstrous creatures. Before that, what I refer to as the essence already existed, but it was greatly strengthened by the Rift.

brightport_bryma35.m: This essence exists within every part of Dhayavar. The soil, the mountains, the creatures, and the people all hold it. The proof lies in the crystals that form inside monsters. These crystals are concentrated forms of essence. Bones are another place where essence gathers most densely. The essence is our world itself. When we take in more of it, we restore what we lose through disease or injury.

brightport_bryma36.m: Not to say it's all the same. Some things, despite containing a high concentration of essence, can be harmful. Such as poisons or diseases that drain our lifeforce. Merely consuming more has no benefit, and indeed there have to be certain attributes or balance.

brightport_bryma37.m: Those statues are intriguing. The light one sees in their vicinity is similar to the descriptions of the blinding light of the false goddess Elythara.

brightport_bryma38.m: Have you had any success with the creatures?
r: As long as you don't bother them again, things should be good now.
I've met with the leader of the lizardman tribe, they demand I return the 13 stolen bones.
I've yet to return the bones.
I returned the bones but I've got one more task to do.
Not yet, I wish to ask you about other things.

brightport_bryma39.m: Lizardmen, again. They've been bothering me for months now. My bread golems can handle a few, but if they all come at once, I'll be in trouble.
r: Maybe I could help with that, what's the story here?

brightport_bryma4.m: Is that any way to speak to someone you just met? So rude! Here - have it. I wasn't intending to keep it anyway. And if you return, leave that attitude outside my cabin.

brightport_bryma40.m: One day, I ventured into that decrepit basement to see what was there. Curious, I began exploring and carelessly ventured down into a cave. Days later, I began hearing the scratching of monstrous claws echoing through the tunnels. Like a warning. It continued for some time, until one day I went down to investigate and found the passage blocked with rubble.
r: I'll see what I can do about those creatures.

brightport_bryma41.m: I appreciate your enthusiasm. The passage down is blocked but if you go deeper into the forest you'll find another statue. The activation word is "Light". Use it, and then find a way to their lair.

brightport_bryma42.m: Suffice to say, those bones are no longer around, I ground them to dust for my bonemeal research and fertilizer experiments.
r: Great, and what am I suppossed to return now?

brightport_bryma42_alt.m: Does this imply they're sentient? No. That can't be...

brightport_bryma42_alt_alt.m: She begins quietly murmuring to herself.

brightport_bryma43.m: No need to look at me like that, if those bones are gone just find more to replace them with.

brightport_bryma44.m: Red or green, their bones look the same. Just slay those red ones along the shore of the lake until you have enough. Here's a few of what I've got left for starters.

brightport_bryma45.m: I see, good luck with that.

brightport_bryma46.m: That is no problem. But how am I supposed to get bones now...
r: I negotiated with the lizardmen, they agree to trade with you the bones of the animals they hunt.
I've solved the main problem. That should be the least of your issues now.

brightport_bryma47.m: You've done a great job, $playername. I have little of value to offer, just these two special potions. I possess very few, so I can't give you more. Use them well.

brightport_bryma48.m: One thing I wish to mention, between Brightport and Charwood, there was a path that travelers would use. When I fled from Feygard, I took that path, but I was stopped by the same phenomenon as in the forest, and had to circle back to the Duleian Road.

brightport_bryma49.m: I later investigated and found another statue, the activation word for that specific one is "Elythara" I hope this information assists you well.

brightport_bryma5.m: It was never my intention to keep it, as it's not particularly useful to me. Here, take it.
r: Thanks! I will make sure it's returned to its place.

brightport_bryma50.m: It is good to see you $playername. what brings you around?
r: I wish to talk about something.

brightport_bryma51.m: That is the gist of my research, which is mostly a theory. I was preparing to publish and discuss it among the scholars of Feygard before I fled.
r: Can we talk about something else?
That's a lot to digest, I think I'll leave now.

brightport_bryma52.m: If you can pacify those creatures and they're truly capable of reason, see if you can come to an understanding. They could supply me with what I need.

brightport_bryma53.m: You're right. I can figure the rest out, $playername. I don't have much to offer, except one of my special potions. I have very few, so use it wisely.

brightport_bryma54.m: For all of it's shortcomings, the cult and her followers fought against necromancy, and many masters of the dark arts perished under their swords. The statues are likely a seal for some evil that dwelt here in ancient times.
r: What's the meaning of that password?

brightport_bryma55.m: I lived in Feygard among the northerners for several years, and the few who do not follow the Shadow bow down to the goddess Elythara. They take great pride in their past. Yet the light they praise has blinded more than it has illuminated. In truth, the Shadow has shown itself to be the more compassionate.
r: Can we talk about something else?
This has left me with more questions than answers.

brightport_bryma56.m: The "Lethgar" password refers to the Lethgar people who lived over two thousand years ago. Perhaps their name was used by those who constructed the statues in remembrance of something.
r: Can we talk about something else?
Interesting, I'll be on my way.

brightport_bryma6.m: You're back again? The forest isn't as quiet as it used to be.
r: I saw a strange creature in the cave under your house. It didn't stick around though.
Can you tell me more about what you know of my brother Andor?
Can you tell me about Andor again?
I'm curious, how did that scroll reach you?
What's with that statue at the entrance of the forest?
Why do you live here in the forest?
You mentioned your bonemeal research, what can you tell me about the potion?
Can you tell me about your bonemeal theory again?

brightport_bryma7.m: That is one of the bread golems I invented, after years of research and study with the great minds of Nor City.

brightport_bryma8.m: It was brought to me by a boy who looked a lot like you.

brightport_bryma9.m: About half a year ago, I was carefully measuring the ingredients for my baking experiments when I heard the door creak. I went to look, and a boy who looked a little older than you introduced himself. I think his name was Andor...

brightport_bryma_alternative_greeting.m: Hello, I am most happy to have someone to talk with.
r: I saw a strange creature in the cave under your house. It didn't stick around though.
Can you tell me more about what you know of my brother Andor?
Can you tell me about Andor again?
I'm curious, how did that scroll get to you?
What's with that statue at the entrance of the forest?
Why do you live here in the forest?
You mentioned your bonemeal research, what can you tell me about the potion?
Can you tell me about your bonemeal theory again?

brightport_bryma_lizarddead.m: Good work $playername. Now I have access to as much bonemeal as I need. Please have these potions, including a special one.

brightport_bryma_lizardexist.m: Sigh, I'm fine with such a violent method. But please finish the work to the end, there are still lizardmen left.

Stanwickquest.5: I arrived at Brightport's school, only to be told that Stanwick is not allowed visitors.
Stanwickquest.10: Janwick, Stanwick's grandfather, mistook me for Andor and asked me to deliver some fresh fruit to Stanwick.
Stanwickquest.15: I was allowed to visit Stanwick.
Stanwickquest.16: I learned that Stanwick is under investigation as the main suspect in the disappearance of an important scroll from the school library.
Stanwickquest.20: Stanwick has something important to tell me about Andor, but I must help him first.
Stanwickquest.25: I agreed to help Stanwick find the culprit responsible for the theft. I should look for clues around the school.
Stanwickquest.30: Milena, the school cook, told me that last year she noticed a dark figure sneaking off from the living quarters.
Stanwickquest.31: Dibella, the lady at the desk at the entrance, told me that Stanwick has a respectable reputation, but as the library supervisor he must be considered a suspect.
Stanwickquest.35: Oswald, the Headmaster, expressed his disbelief that Stanwick is guilty of the theft and accepted my help in finding the document, whilst insisting that it be returned to him.
Stanwickquest.40: Frederich, the history teacher who moved in from Feygard, believes Stanwick is associated with "Those Nor City savages" and was told by them to steal the document.
Stanwickquest.45: Franz, the math teacher, told me that the most logical thing to do is to investigate the library, which is sealed. I must find a way to access it.
Stanwickquest.46: I asked the Headmaster for access to the library, but he denied my request.
Stanwickquest.47: I stole the library key from the Headmaster's desk while he was distracted. Hopefully there will be no consequences.
Stanwickquest.50: Counterfeit, a thieves guild member in the basement of the Brightport warehouse, gave me a copy of the library key.
Stanwickquest.55: In the library's basement archive, I found a record of a baker named Bryma requesting to read the secret scroll, but she was denied. I should seek out her whereabouts.
Stanwickquest.60: Richimor, the old man sitting by the lake shore in Brightport, was an acquaintance of Bryma. He said she left Brightport many years ago and did not tell him where she went, but she left a large part of her research material at his house. I should check it.
Stanwickquest.65: Inside Richimor's house, I found a bundle of papers left by Bryma. In there, amongst the trivial writings, one paper stood out as it talked about four strange statues in the vicinity of Brightport.
Stanwickquest.66: I discovered a strange statue in the forest south of Brightport, with several indecipherable symbols. Perhaps this is one of the statues mentioned in the writings of Bryma.
Stanwickquest.70: I examined a statue north of Brightport. Carved into the statue were the symbols for the letters L and H.
Stanwickquest.75: I examined a statue southeast of Brightport. Carved into the statue were the symbols for the letters T and E.
Stanwickquest.80: I examined a statue far west of Brightport. Carved into the statue were the symbols for the letters A, G, and R.
Stanwickquest.84: The puzzle is proving itself to be very difficult. I should return to the library in Brightport to search for clues
Stanwickquest.85: I spoke the activation word to the statue in the forest, and can now move further.
Stanwickquest.86: Inside the forest was a cabin, in which I found Bryma and some strange creature made of bread.
Stanwickquest.92: I received the secret scroll from Bryma. I should return it to the headmaster now.
Stanwickquest.95: I threatened Bryma to make her hand over the scroll. She gave it to me as she did not intend to keep it anyway.
Stanwickquest.96: I returned the secret scroll to the Headmaster and Stanwick was cleared of all suspicion. I should inform him.
Stanwickquest.97: I did not receive any reward.
Stanwickquest.100: I received a reward from the Headmaster for having returned the scroll.
Stanwickquest.110: I informed Stanwick and he was relieved to hear the news.

charwood1.10: I heard a rumor that some mining town in the Charwood forest, northwest of the Foaming Flask tavern, has had some troubles recently. I should try to find the Charwood cabin and find out what has happened.
charwood1.11: I heard someone mention that the mining town of Charwood heights has had some troubles recently. I should search for the Charwood cabin in the forest northwest of the Foaming Flask tavern.
charwood1.19: I have found the Charwood cabin in the forest northwest of the Foaming Flask tavern.
charwood1.20: Maevalia in the Charwood cabin told me a story about how their mining settlement was attacked by some monsters, forcing them to flee down the mountain. They are still missing several of their friends and relatives from the Charwood heights, either killed or captured by the monsters.
charwood1.21: In particular, Maevalia mentions four people that are greatly missed; their former leader Morenavia, their weapons trainer Falothen, the healer Ayell and their armorer Fayvara.
charwood1.30: I have agreed to help the people of Charwood find their missing people.
charwood1.35: The guard outside the Charwood cabin allowed me to enter the hills ahead. I should keep to the east and then head north.
charwood1.40: I encountered one of the monsters that Maevalia spoke of. The monster spoke of someone or something called 'The Thukuzun'.
charwood1.41: I have found Falothen, the weapons trainer of the Charwood heights, and freed him from the restraints that held him. He will try to make his way back to the Charwood cabin himself.
charwood1.42: I have found some skeletal remains, containing a ring with the insignia 'Morenavia'. This must be the former leader of the Charwood hills.
charwood1.43: I have found the armorer Fayvara, and freed her from the restraints that held her. She will try to make her way back to the Charwood cabin herself.
charwood1.44: I have found some skeletal remains, containing a ring with the insignia 'Ayell'. This must be the remains of the Charwood hills healer that Maevalia mentioned.
charwood1.50: Maevalia thanked me for finding out what happened to the four people that she told me about, but was really sad to hear about the fate of Morenavia and Ayell. Both the weapons trainer Falothen and the armorer Fayvara made it back to the Charwood cabin safely.
charwood1.60: She told me that both Falothen and Fayvara are anxious to see me, in the basement of the Charwood cabin. I should go see them at once.
charwood1.65: Falothen was happy to see me again, and in return offered to train me in better handling of one weapon type. He can teach me better handling of one or two handed swords, daggers, blunt weapons, axes, or unarmed combat. I'll have to chose my preference and let him know.
charwood1.70: Falothen has taught me how to better handle one handed swords.
charwood1.71: Falothen has taught me how to better handle two handed swords.
charwood1.72: Falothen has taught me how to better handle daggers.
charwood1.73: Falothen has taught me how to better handle blunt weapons.
charwood1.74: Falothen has taught me how to better handle axes.
charwood1.75: Falothen has taught me how to be better at fighting unarmed, without weapons.
charwood1.76: Falothen has taught me how to better handle polearms.
charwood1.80: Falothen offered me the chance to learn about the other weapon types, but to teach me, he needs 5000 gold and two Oegyth crystals for each skill that I want to get better at.
charwood1.90: Fayvara thanked me for rescuing her, and in return offered to train me in better handling of one type of armor. She can teach me better handling of shields, light armor, heavy armor or or unarmored combat. I'll have to chose my preference and let her know.
charwood1.91: Fayvara has taught me how to better handle shields.
charwood1.92: Fayvara has taught me how to better handle light armor.
charwood1.93: Fayvara has taught me how to better handle heavy armor.
charwood1.94: Fayvara has taught me how to better fighting unarmored, without wearing any armor.
charwood1.100: Fayvara offered me the chance to learn about the other armor types, but to teach me, she needs 6000 gold and two Oegyth crystals for each skill that I want to get better at.
charwood1.110: I have been taught one weapon type skill and one armor type skill from Falothen and Fayvara. I should go see Maevalia again.
charwood1.115: Maevalia thanked me for helping the people of Charwood.

brightport_lizard.1: In the rundown mysterious basement behind Bryma's house, I encountered a humanoid green creature that fled beyond a pile of cave rubble.
brightport_lizard.5: When I questioned Bryma about the creature, she explained that lizardmen live in the caves beneath her house and have been bothering her for some time.
brightport_lizard.10: I agreed to help Bryma with her problem. She shared the activation phrase for another statue leading deeper into the forest.
brightport_lizard.15: After navigating through the caves, I reached an open chamber beyond the rubble, where I found the lizardman again.
brightport_lizard.20: The lizardman regarded me suspiciously, calling me an intruder. He claimed Bryma had been stealing bones from their ancestral tomb, which his people were trying to recover.
brightport_lizard.25: I attacked the lizardman, but my attack merely grazed it, before it fled deeper into the caves.
brightport_lizard.30: I tried to calm Emyro's worries. He hesitated but told me to visit their leader before disappearing into the shadows.
brightport_lizard.32: I tracked down and killed the lizardmen's leader, Elyzard.
brightport_lizard.35: I killed the rest of those slimy lizards. Bryma can now rest free.
brightport_lizard.36: I received a reward from Bryma for getting rid of the creatures.
brightport_lizard.40: To earn the trust of the tribe's leader, Elyzard. I swore to return the 13 stolen bones.
brightport_lizard.50: To my astonishment, I discovered that Bryma had ground the bones into dust for her research and fertilizer experiments.
brightport_lizard.55: Bryma suggested I retrieve replacement bones from other sources. She advised hunting the hostile red lizardmen in the nearby area until I could gather the required amount.
brightport_lizard.60: I delivered the bones to Elyzard, who acknowledged my effort but requested one more task. He instructed me to visit the Shadow Chaplain's cave for further guidance.
brightport_lizard.65: From Dominio, the Shadow chaplain, I learned that beasts of darkness were attacking the tribe from an ancient ruin on the western side of the cave.
brightport_lizard.70: To stop the attacks, I was tasked with destroying two crystals within the ruins by chanting the phrase "Kazaul thu'um kha'zan" before striking them.
brightport_lizard.90: Elyzard recognized my effort, and rewarded me with a trinbal artifact.
brightport_lizard.95: I offered the lizardmen a deal of cooperation to supply Bryma with animal bones as a sign of mutual respect.
brightport_lizard.100: Bryma agreed to stop intruding on the lizardmen's tomb, as they promised to supply her with bones for her research.
brightport_lizard.110: Bryma agreed to stop intruding on the lizardmen's tomb.

andor.1: My father Mikhail says that Andor has not been home since yesterday. I should go look for him in the village.
andor.10: Leonid tells me that he saw Andor talking to Gruil. I should go ask Gruil if he knows more.
andor.20: Gruil wants me to bring him a poison gland. Then he might talk more. He tells me that some poisonous snakes have such a gland.
andor.30: Gruil tells me that Andor was looking for someone called Umar. I should go ask his friend Gaela in Fallhaven to the east.
andor.40: I talked to Gaela in Fallhaven. He tells me to go see Bucus and ask about the Thieves' Guild.
andor.50: Bucus has allowed me to enter the hatch in the derelict house in Fallhaven. I should go talk to Umar.
andor.51: Umar in the Fallhaven Thieves' Guild recognized me, but must have me confused with Andor. Apparently, Andor has been to see him.
andor.55: Umar told me that Andor went to see a potion maker called Lodar. I should search for his hideaway.
andor.61: I heard a story in Loneford, where it seemed like Andor had been in Loneford, and that he might have had something to do with the illness that the people are suffering from there. I am not sure if it actually was Andor. If it was Andor, why would he have made the people of Loneford ill?
andor.62: Andor might have gone to do some business with a rich man in Brimhaven after he left Loneford.
andor.65: It looks like Andor was involved in the destruction of the Brimhaven dam.
andor.70: I have found the potion-maker Lodar, and heard his story about Andor. Andor went to visit Lodar in his hideaway to get a sample of something called Narwood extract. Lodar happened to notice that there was someone travelling together with Andor, that hid among the trees and did not seem to want Lodar to spot him.
andor.71: Shortly after Andor and the person he was travelling with had left, strange things started to happen in the woods around Lodar's hideaway, and Lodar himself seemed to be affected by it somehow. Lodar believes that something disturbed the tomb below his cabin, and awoke the Hira'zinn.
andor.72: Since I helped Lodar defeat the Hira'zinn, he promised to help me in return. He gave me a piece of paper that should allow me to enter the Valanyr temple of the Shadow in Nor City. He told me to seek out lady Lydalon in the temple for further assistance.
andor.80: All clues so far as to where Andor went point to Nor City. I should travel to Nor City by following the Duleian road to the southeast and look for more clues there.
andor.85: Andor may have been in Stoutford.
andor.86: Andor had something to do with the demon under the church in Stoutford.
andor.90: At Castle Guynmart I learned from Steward Unkorh that some time ago Andor was also there as a guest.
andor.92: Unkorh gave me the bonemeal potion box that Andor had given him for safekeeping.
andor.100: While exploring the town of Sullengard, I so happened to stumble upon my mother and my aunt to whom I have never met. Mother has insisted that I go home so we can talk.
andor.110: After talking with mother back at home, she and I tried to brainstorm about where Andor could be. She reminded me about Andor's friend Stanwick who lives in Brightport. We agreed that going to talk to him might be the next logical thing to do.
andor.120: In the dungeons of Laeroth manor, Kotheses, the torturer, mentioned that he had taught Andor the basics of torturing.
andor.125: Vaelric confirmed that Andor visited him recently. Andor sought to learn Vaelric's skills and left quickly, clutching what he came for. His actions raise more questions about his intentions.
andor.126: In Brightport, I was finally able to meet Stanwick, but due to his hazy memory, he was not able to help me learn anything about the whereabouts of Andor.
andor.127: Regaining his peace of mind after I helped him, Stanwick said he'll tell me more about Andor, once he gathers his thoughts.
andor.128: Stanwick gave me a signet ring that I should show to his father. Jorwick, in Nor City.
andor.130: Andor was trying to find out from Seraphina about terrible monsters in the hideout near the place with the larval burrowers.
andor.131: Elysa in the Brightport's thieves guild told me that Andor has bought a map to the sewers of Feygard.
andor.132: While investigating the Brightport theft I learned from Bryma that Andor was the one who stole the important document, and brought it to her in exchange for her alchemy knowledge.
andor.140: I saw Andor in the mountains of Galmore. We were able to exchange a few words before he disappeared again.
andor.145: I met Andor on the road to Feygard, where he was buying food from Rosmara. He disappeared again.
andor.147: I met Andor on the road to Nor City, where he was buying supplies from Alynndir. He disappeared again.
andor.910: I decided to settle down on the top of Mt. Galmore. For this I needed to find a rich and discreet man to rebuild the ruins according to my wishes. Andor will now have to go and find himself.
